records.title: Need for increasing family income limit for medical treatment under Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme.
details:
Shri Golla Baburao:
There is no doubt that Government is doing very good
work in healthcare sector, be it through Ayushman Bharat, Jan Aushadhi Stores,
etc. And, at the same time, Government is also implementing Dr. Ambedkar
Medical Aid Scheme for SC/ST. The objective of the scheme is to provide
medical treatment facility to SC/STs suffering from serious diseases relating
to kidney, heart, liver, cancer, brain or any other life threatening diseases
and it also includes organ transplant and spinal surgery. Poor people of
SC/ST are grateful to Hon?ble Prime Minister for this scheme. But, our
concern is relating to family income limit fixed to avail the benefits of this
scheme. Annul family income is fixed at Rs.3 lakhs per annum which is
very, very less and there is an urgent need to revise this. 
Secondly, scheme guidelines say that 100% of the estimated cost of treatment
will be given. But, at the same time, it also puts a ceiling on
treatment, such as, Rs.1.25 lakhs for heart surgery; Rs.3.5 lakhs for kidney
surgery; Rs.1.75 lakhs for cancer surgery, chemo and radio therapy; Rs.1.5
lakhs for brain surgery; Rs.1 lakh for spinal injury, etc.
Hence, I appeal to the Government to
increase annual family income limit to Rs.8 lakhs as has been done in the case
of OBC creamy layer which will help many poor SC/STs.
(ENDS)

records.title: Request for release of domestic LPG connections under PM-UjjwalaYojana to poor women in Andhra Pradesh.
details:
Shri Golla Baburao: 
PM announced giving 25 lakh more domestic
LPG connections under PM-Ujjwala Yojana to poor women during 2025-26 to clear
pending applications. PMUY is providing LPG connections to adult women from
poor households and so far 10.33 crore connections are given.? This has been
appreciated by women who otherwise suffering by burning solid fuels like wood,
dung and crop residues.? Women preferring LPG gas since it lowers indoor air
pollution leading to better respiratory health.? Secondly, everybody
appreciating that GOI is giving Rs.300 subsidy per cylinder for 9 refills to
ease financial burden on poor women. 9.72 lakh connections are given to poor
women in AP under PM-Ujjwala for which they are grateful to hon.PM.? Out of
these, 1.74 lakh belongs to SC/ST communities.? But, there are still 60,000
applications pending from poor women for LPG connections from AP.? All
applicants are eagerly waiting that they would get connection out of 25 lakh
approved. Hence, I request Government to consider all 60,000 applications from
AP and provide poor women LPG connections at the earliest.? I also request for
increasing the LPG subsidy from Rs. 300 now being given per cylinder to Rs. 500
which will go a long way in easing financial burden on women.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over hiring staff in Signal & Telecommunication Department in Railways on contract basis.
details:
Shri Golla Baburao: Safety is the biggest concern and there is no doubt Railways is taking
various measures, including Kavach, to provide foolproof safety for passengers
and its network. The results are encouraging ? accidents have reduced from 135
in 2014-15 to just 31 in 2024-25. It has all happened due to policies of
Railways and hard work being done by regular safety category employees of
Railways. But, surprisingly, Railway Board issued a Circular to GMs of 4
Railway Zones asking to hire people on contract to take care of modern
signaling, telecommunications and maintenance of safety department. This
move has shocked not only Railway Unions but also others. Safety department has
complex interlock mechanisms and advanced electronic systems. So,
contract workers, I strongly believe, as supervisors, field engineers and
technicians may not be fully appropriate for train operations and passengers?
safety. Railway Board is aware that complex and interlocking of signal
and telecom departments need high and intensive training of nearly 2 years at
Signal & Telecommunication Training Centre (STTCs) and Indian
Railway Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications
(IRISET). And, Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) in its investigation report
of collision of Mysuru-Dharbhanga Bagmati Express flagged a similar concern.
Hence, I appeal to the Government to withdraw the circular to appoint contract
workers in safety departments and, instead, appoint regular employees.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand to increase family income limit under Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme.
details:
Shri Golla Baburao: Government is implementing Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid
Scheme to provide medical treatment to patients suffering from serious health
problems relating to kidney, heart, liver, cancer, brain etc., for SC/ST. 
It is a very good scheme for poor SC/STs. Under this scheme, 100% of the
estimated cost of the treatment is given to the concerned hospital. But,
there are various limitations and one of them is the family income of SC/ST
which should not exceed Rs. 3 lakhs per annum. Secondly, if one looks at
the money given for various surgeries/treatment, it appears to be insufficient.
For example, the following amounts are being given under Dr. Ambedkar Medical
Aid Scheme: 1. Heart Surgery ? Rs. 1.25 lakhs.
2. Kidney Surgery ? Rs.
3.5 lakhs. 3. Cancer ? Rs. 1.75 lakhs. 4. Brain Surgery ? Rs. 1.5 lakhs.
5. Kidney Transplant ? Rs. 3.5 lakhs. 6. 
Spinal Surgery ? Rs. 1 lakh. The rates for various surgeries are fraction of
the real cost for important surgeries and treatment. Government is saying
that 100% of the estimated cost of the treatment is directly released to the
concerned hospital. But, the real estimated cost is much, much
more. Not only this, the income limit fixed for family is also too low,
which is Rs. 3 lakhs per annum of family income. Hence, I appeal to the
Government to revise the family income limit to Rs. 10 Lakhs and also increase
the limits for various treatment/surgeries to, at least, at par with the rates
of CGHS.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over issues faced by Vizag Steel Plant (R.I.N.L.).
details:
Shri Golla Baburao: Being India?s first
shore-based integrated steel plant, RINL (Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited) was
earning profits and had positive net worth.? But, subsequently, it started
incurring losses due to not having captive mines.? RINL is buying iron ore from
open market at higher price, unlike other PSU steel companies which have captive
mines and enjoy cost advantage. Secondly, RINL is borrowing money @14% interest
for working capital.? As a result the cost of production has gone up, thereby
affecting its profitability.? RINL has been appealing for allocation of iron
ore mines under Section 17A(2A) of the MMDR Act, 2015.? But, no significant
progress has happened so far.? I, therefore, demand that time has come to allot
iron ore mines to RINL to make it profitable. Further, the employees of RINL
are also facing issues of wage revision, promotion policy, recruitment, delayed
payment of salaries and cuts in salary, perks, HRA etc. Recently, RINL has
introduced two Voluntary Retirement Schemes & nearly 1500 employees have
been given VRS.? The Andhra Pradesh Assembly has also passed unanimous resolution
against privatization of RINL.? Steel Ministry says that CCEA approved 100%
RINL disinvestment. Hence, I make following demands from the Government:- Immediate
allocation of iron ore mines to RINL. Stop retrenchment of employees. Provide
more money for working capital. Merge RINL with SAIL.
(ENDS)

records.title: Reconsider the Privatisation and Disinvestment of the RINL Vizag Steel Plant
details:
Shri
Golla Baburao:
RINL, Visakhapatnam steel plant was set-up only after a decade-long public
agitation of "Visakha Ukku-AndhrulaHakku". Over 40 people were killed
in different parts of the then undivided Andhra Pradesh during this agitation.
About 1 lakh people are dependent on the steel plant, including 17,000
permanent employees and 16,000 contractual employees. Since December 2020, the
company is making a monthly profit of ₹200 Crores. The steel plant, launched with 1.7
million tonnes capacity was later expanded to 7.3 million tonnes without any
financial support from the Centre. Therefore, it makes no economic sense to
privatise the steel plant.?? As per the Union Ministry of Steel?s report,
Vizag Steel Plant is the only steel-manufacturing PSE in the country that has
no captive iron ore mine. The losses were majorly due to the lack of captive
mines due to which the RINL has to procure the iron ore at market price. Taking
into account the pride, sentiment and interests of people in Andhra, I would
request the Central Government to reconsider this decision of privatising Vizag
Steel Plant.???????? 
??????????????????????? 
(Ends)
